edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De praescriptionibus adversus haereticos, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Quin potius memores simus tam dominicarum pronuntiationum, quam apostolicarum litterarum, quae nobis et futuras haereses praenuntiarunt, et fugiendas praefinierunt; et sicut esse illas non expavescimus, ita posse id, propter quod fugiendae sunt, non miremur. Instruit Dominus multos esse venturos, sub pellibus ovium, rapaces lupos. Quaenam istae sunt pelles ovium, nisi nominis christiani extrinsecus superficies? qui lupi rapaces, nisi sensus et spiritus subdoli, ad infestandum gregem Christi extrinsecus delitescentes? qui pseudoprophetae sunt, nisi falsi praedicatores? qui pseudapostoli, nisi adulteri evangelizatores? qui antichristi interim et semper, nisi Christi rebelles? Nunc sunt haereses, non minus doctrinarum perversitate Ecclesiam lacessentes, quam tunc Antichristus persecutionum atrocitate persequetur: nisi quod persecutio et martyras facit, haeresis apostatas tantum. Et ideo haereses quoque oportebat esse, ut probabiles quique manifestarentur, tam qui in persecutionibus steterint, quam qui ad haereses non exorbitaverint. Neque enim eos probabiles intelligi juvat, qui in haeresim fidem demutant: sicut ex diverso sibi interpretantur, quia dixit alibi: Omnia examinate, quod bonum est tenete. Quasi non liceat, omnibus male examinatis, in electionem alicujus mali impingere per errorem.
thought_title: Remembering the Lord's and Apostles' Warnings
pass_a_gloss: Rather let us be mindful of both the Lord's pronouncements and the apostolic letters, which have announced to us both future heresies and defined those to be avoided; and just as we do not fear that those heresies exist, so let us not be surprised that they can do that for which they are to be avoided. The Lord teaches that many will come, in sheep's skins, rapacious wolves. What are these sheep's skins, if not the external surface of the Christian name? Who are the rapacious wolves, if not the cunning senses and spirits lurking externally to harass the flock of Christ? Who are the false prophets, if not the false preachers? Who are the false apostles, if not the adulterous evangelists? Who are the antichrists, if not the rebels against Christ? Now there are heresies, no less troubling the Church with the perversity of doctrines than the Antichrist will then persecute with the atrocity of persecutions; except that persecution makes martyrs, but heresy makes only apostates. And therefore heresies also had to exist, so that the approved ones might be revealed, both those who will stand in persecutions and those who will not deviate into heresies. For it does not help to consider them approved who change their faith into heresy: just as, on the other hand, they interpret for themselves, because He said elsewhere: Examine all things, hold fast what is good. As if it were not allowed, having poorly examined all things, to fall into the choice of some evil through error.

choices.why: describing the action of the wolves
describing the cause of falling into evil

pass_b_english: We should rather keep in mind both the Lord's pronouncements and the apostolic letters, which foretold future heresies to us and defined them as things to be avoided (Matt 7:15); and just as we do not fear that those heresies exist, so we should not be surprised that they can do the very thing for which they are to be avoided. The Lord teaches that many will come in sheep's clothing as rapacious wolves. What are these sheepskins, if not the external surface of the Christian name? Who are the rapacious wolves, if not cunning minds and spirits lurking outwardly to harass Christ's flock? Who are the false prophets, if not false preachers? Who are the false apostles, if not adulterous evangelists? Who are the antichrists, both now and always, if not rebels against Christ? Heresies exist now, troubling the Church with the perversity of their doctrines no less than the Antichrist will persecute it then with the atrocity of his persecutions; the only difference is that persecution makes martyrs, while heresy makes only apostates. And therefore heresies also had to exist, so that the approved might be revealed — both those who stand firm in persecutions and those who do not deviate into heresies. For it does no good to regard as approved those who change their faith into heresy: just as, on the other hand, they interpret the matter for themselves, because He said elsewhere: "Examine all things; hold fast to what is good" (1 Thess 5:21). As if it were not possible, after examining all things poorly, to fall by error into the choice of some evil.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the necessary scripture citations (Matt 7:15 and 1 Thess 5:21) which correspond to the content of the Latin 'sub pellibus ovium' and 'Omnia examinate, quod bonum est tenete'. Pass A is a faithful gloss. All nuances regarding agency (persecution vs heresy) and modality are preserved.
